::: {#def-chi-square-test}
#### Pearson's chi-square test of independence

Let a contingency table have $r$ rows and $c$ columns,
with observed count $O_{ij}$ in row $i$ and column $j$,
row totals $R_i$, column totals $C_j$, and grand total $n$.
The **expected count** in cell $(i, j)$ under independence is

$$E_{ij} \eqdef \frac{R_i \, C_j}{n}.$$

**Pearson's chi-square test** of the null hypothesis
that the row and column variables are independent
uses the statistic

$$X^2 \eqdef \sum_{i=1}^r \sum_{j=1}^c \frac{(O_{ij} - E_{ij})^2}{E_{ij}}.$$

Its p-value is $\Pr(W \ge X^2)$,
where $W$ has the $\chi^2_{(r-1)(c-1)}$ distribution
([chi-square distribution](inference.qmd#def-chi-square-dist)).
:::
